description: Instead of building a basic static map, we are building TerraTwin, a geospatial search engine that converts real NASA elevation and spectral rasters (LOLA, HiRISE, Copernicus DEM) into spatial feature vectors to find the most accurate Earth testing sites for Moon and Mars hardware, complete with a synchronised 3D split-screen viewer and physics discrepancy warnings .
summary:
GeoTwin-X is an advanced aerospace planetary analogue search engine developed for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge. Field-testing rovers, spacesuits, and In-Situ Resource Utilisation (ISRU) systems on Earth is vital before planetary launch, yet researchers have historically been limited to a handful of repetitive textbook sites evaluated through superficial guesswork.
GeoTwin-X addresses the challenge by connecting 10 Mars regions and 10 Moon Artemis regions (divided into 43 geological sub-parts) to a global multi-continental database of 200 contiguous km×10km grid sectors (20,000 km^2) across 7 continents and 7 biomes. Using authentic NASA, ESA, USGS, and ISRO digital elevation models, GeoTwin-X performs mathematically authentic multi-objective cosine similarity matching across 10-dimensional topographic feature spaces (slope, roughness, curvature, hypsometry).
Features include dual synchronised 3D WebGL terrain viewports, dynamic 3×3 hectare cluster analysis, and the NASA Breakdown Boundary Scorecard, which transparently identifies where Earth analogies break down physically (gravity, atmosphere, biogenic contamination) alongside field deployment logistics. GeoTwin-X bridges theoretical planetary science and operational field engineering, de-risking multi-million-dollar space exploration missions.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

GeoTwin-X acts as an intelligent matchmaker between off-world target destinations on Mars and the Moon and authentic analog terrains across the Earth.

The user selects a target planetary body (Mars or Moon), a specific region (e.g., Jezero Crater or Shackleton Crater), and an exact geological sub-part (e.g., Delta Scarp or Permanent Shadowed Cold Trap). The engine dynamically slices the authentic raster (such as NASA's 20m Jezero CTX DEM) to compute an elevation profile, micro-topographic slope gradients, Riley's Terrain Roughness Index (TRI), Laplacian profile curvature, hypsometric integrals, and geomorphic proxies.

These metrics form a standardized 10-dimensional feature vector. Using scikit-learn, the engine computes normalized cosine similarity against a pre-compiled global grid database of 200 real 10km×10km sectors across 24 Earth geological provinces. The system supports three operational query modes:

  1. Mobility & Traversability Mode: Prioritizes obstacle roughness (TRI) and wheel slip hazards (>15∘ slopes).
  2. ISRU & Mineralogy Mode: Prioritizes volcanic basalt textures, profile curvature, and sedimentary delta terraces.
  3. Regional Context Mode: Prioritizes macro-hypsometry and regional relief variance.

Results are displayed in an aerospace-themed Mission Control HUD featuring dual synchronized 3D WebGL terrain viewports, dynamic 3×3 hectare cluster analysis, candidate rankings, the NASA Breakdown Boundary Scorecard, and expedition logistics.

What benefits does it have?

  1. Mathematical Objectivity: Eliminates biased, subjective site selection. Every ranking is derived from reproducible linear algebra over real satellite elevation rasters.
  2. Landing Footprint Granularity: Through its 3×3 hectare cluster analysis, rovers are evaluated not on single mathematical coordinate points, but within a realistic 9-sector landing zone.
  3. Physics Breakdown Transparency: Identifies the physical boundaries where Earth analogies diverge (e.g., Mars normal traction reduction of 62.1%, rotor tip speed scaling of 7.8×7.8 in thin atmosphere) so engineers can build appropriate test rigs.
  4. Actionable Logistics: Provides runway lengths, medevac flight times, communications availability, and permit authorities to make expeditions actionable.

What is the intended impact of the project?

To streamline and de-risk the testing phase for lunar and martian surface missions. By matching rover locomotion, autonomous navigation, and drilling systems against the most geologically and topographically accurate terrestrial analogues available, space agencies reduce hardware failure risks on flight missions.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Backend: Python 3.10+, FastAPI (asynchronous REST API), Uvicorn (ASGI server), Pydantic (data validation).
  • Machine Learning & Math: Scikit-Learn (pairwise vector cosine similarity), NumPy (matrix transformations), SciPy ndimage (Horn's finite-difference slope convolution, Riley TRI roughness, Laplacian curvature).
  • Geospatial Processing: GDAL / Rasterio (GeoTIFF slicing, windowed reads, affine transformations, coordinate reprojection).
  • Frontend HUD: HTML5, CSS3 Aerospace Design System, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Three.js (r128 WebGL 3D rendering engine, OrbitControls camera synchronization), HTML5 2.5D Canvas fallback.
  • Cloud & Hosting: Google Colab, Cloudflare Quick Tunnel, Render.com.

How is your project creative?

  • Dual Synchronized 3D Topography Viewports: Pans, rotates, and zooms in both target and Earth viewports simultaneously at a 1:1 scale, giving flight teams an immediate visual sense of terrain comparability.
  • Dynamic 3×3 Hectare Matrix: Connects primary landing sites to 8 surrounding compass sectors (NW, N, NE, W, E, SW, S, SE) to assess traversability corridors.
  • Honest Breakdown Scorecards: Unlike tools that claim "perfect 100% matches," GeoTwin-X embraces scientific reality by showing engineers exactly where Earth analogues fail and how to mitigate those failures experimentally.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Zero Synthetic Data Integrity: Ensuring no hardcoded numbers or fake scores appear anywhere in the pipeline.
  • Browser Performance & Hardware Inclusivity: Preventing multi-gigabyte raster files from freezing local browsers by compiling lightweight, pre-computed vector indices.
  • Fault-Tolerant Resiliency: Implementing smart coordinate auto-clamping so out-of-bounds user entries never crash the web server.
